title: Hungarian Stuffed Peppers
subtitle: Pork and rice stuffed peppers in a paprika tomato sauce
excerpt: Green peppers filled with seasoned pork mince and rice, cooked slowly in a sweet paprika tomato sauce until the filling is tender and the sauce is thick. A Hungarian home-cooking staple.
sourceNotes: Hungarian töltött paprika tradition, a central dish in the national cuisine, particularly associated with the Tisza river region.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in the sauce in an airtight container. Defrost overnight and reheat gently on the hob with a lid on.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a double batch of the sauce and freeze half separately for a quick weeknight dinner base.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made a day ahead and kept in the sauce in the fridge. Reheat covered in the oven at 180C.

content.text: Stuffed peppers in Hungary are always cooked in a paprika tomato sauce, not baked dry. The sauce keeps the filling moist and the peppers soft. Use pale green pointed peppers for the most authentic result, but bell peppers work fine.

items.prepNote: tops cut off and seeds removed

content.text: Heat the oven to 180C. Make the filling: mix the pork mince, rinsed rice, grated onion, garlic, paprika, egg, salt and pepper in a bowl until combined.
Fill each pepper three-quarters full with the pork mixture. The rice will expand as it cooks, so do not overfill. Set the peppers in the roasting tin, cut side up.
Make the sauce: pour the tinned tomatoes and stock into the large saucepan. Add the tomato puree, paprika and sugar. Stir and bring to a simmer for 5 minutes.
Pour the sauce over and around the peppers. It should come about halfway up the sides. Season the sauce with salt.
Cover the roasting tin tightly with foil. Bake for 50 minutes.
Remove the foil and bake for a further 20 minutes until the sauce is thick and the tops of the peppers are lightly coloured.
Rest for 5 minutes. Spoon the sauce into bowls, sit a pepper on top and add a generous spoonful of soured cream.

items.symptom: The filling has not cooked through.
items.cause: The peppers were packed too tightly and the heat did not penetrate.
items.fix: Return to the oven covered for a further 15 minutes. Check with a skewer; it should meet no resistance.

items.cause: The sauce level was too low or the foil had a gap.
items.fix: Add 100ml of hot stock, reseal the foil tightly and cook for another 15 minutes.

items.cause: The tomatoes were very watery or the sauce quantity was high.
items.fix: Remove the peppers and simmer the sauce on the hob for 10 minutes to reduce. Return the peppers and serve.
